checks.note: Acme Fastening is never named; it is called "a competitor." HomeMax is named, but it is a customer, so the rule isn't broken.
Bullet 1 covers the 61% two-customer concentration and HomeMax not renewing a contract that expires in Q1.
Bullet 2 ties the 38% margin to the 36% covenant on the $20M line renewing in December and notes the 2-point cushion. Bullet 3 covers the drop from 42% and the 15% steel cost rise.

Every figure comes from the report, and the 2-point cushion is correctly derived. "No stated offset" is an accurate inference, not an invented fact. The heading "Covenant breach" overstates things a little, since no breach has happened yet, but the bullet frames it as a risk.

unasked_content: The parenthetical "(Note: this names a customer, not a competitor.)" in bullet 1 is meta-commentary about the instructions. It adds clutter to a list that was supposed to be clean.
The heading "Covenant breach" suggests a breach has already happened. In fact, margin is still above the 36% minimum, so this is a risk, not an event.
